subject: Information Theory
title: Turbo Codes
description: A fast breakdown of Turbo Codes for builders.

hook.text: In 1993, two French engineers stunned the coding world: their turbo codes came within 0.7 dB of Shannon's limit.

buildup.text: Turbo codes use two convolutional encoders in parallel, separated by an interleaver that scrambles the data.

discovery.text: The decoder iterates: each decoder passes soft information to the other, refining estimates in ping-pong fashion.

twist.text: Iterative decoding was the key. Individual codes were modest; together they reached near-Shannon performance.

climax.text: Turbo codes were adopted for 3G/4G cellular, deep-space communication, and WiMAX. They changed engineering overnight.

punchline.text: Two weak codes cooperating beat one strong code alone.

quiz.question: What was the key innovation in turbo codes?
options: Iterative decoding between two parallel encoders
